Thanks for reaching out. This is a policy/informational question about our data retention practices rather than a code issue, so no file changes are needed here. Our support/security team will follow up directly with details on how long uploaded import files are retained and when they are deleted after processing.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits input on `"
"` only (`text.split("
")`), without stripping carriage returns. Files exported from Windows tools typically use CRLF line endings, so each line (including the header) retains a trailing ``. This causes the column count/shape comparison to mismatch, triggering `errors.rowShape` ("Malformed row...") on row 1 even though the file is well-formed. The parser should normalize line endings (e.g. strip `` or split on `/
|
/`) before splitting into rows.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

The issue isn't actually in the CSV writer — it's upstream in the dedupe logic. `dedupeKey` builds its key from `[t.date, t.amount, t.description]` only, so two transactions that differ solely by currency produce the same key and one gets dropped as a duplicate during ingest (see `src/ingest/dedupe.ts`). This went unnoticed until transactions started carrying a currency field in 3.2.0. The fix should include `currency` in the dedupe key.

label: bug
file: src/notifications/templates.ts

The password reset email builds its link from `BASE_URL`, which falls back to `http://localhost:3000` whenever `PUBLIC_URL` isn't set in the environment. It looks like the deployed environment is missing that `PUBLIC_URL` config (likely since last week's release), so every reset email links to localhost instead of the real app URL. Needs to either ensure `PUBLIC_URL` is set correctly in production config, or fix the fallback/resolution logic in templates.ts.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the file content with `text.split("\n")` only, so it doesn't account for Windows-style CRLF line endings. When a file uses `\r\n`, the trailing `\r` remains attached to the last field of each line, which throws off the column count comparison against the header and triggers `errors.rowShape` ("Malformed row"). Since finance switched to a new Windows-based export tool, their files likely now use CRLF endings, explaining why every upload fails at row 1. The fix should normalize/strip `\r` characters (e.g. split on `/\r?\n/` or strip `\r` from each line) before validating column counts.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

The merging isn't happening in the CSV writer — it's the ingest-time dedupe logic. `dedupeKey` builds its key from `date`, `amount`, and `description` only (src/ingest/dedupe.ts:8), so two transactions that differ only by currency hash to the same key and one gets dropped as a duplicate before it ever reaches the CSV export step. Since 3.2.0 added currency to transactions, this collision now surfaces for cases like the EUR/USD pair described here. The key should incorporate `currency` as well.

This is answered in our architecture documentation: after a successful import, the worker deletes the uploaded file from object storage. Failed uploads are retained for a limited period (see `FAILED_UPLOAD_RETENTION_DAYS` in `src/ingest/worker.ts`, currently 7 days) before being purged. See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` ("What happens to uploaded files") for the full explanation. No code changes are needed here.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

The CSV export isn't actually merging rows at write time — the rows are being deduplicated earlier, during ingestion. `dedupeKey` in `src/ingest/dedupe.ts` builds its key from `date`, `amount` and `description` only:

```
export const dedupeKey = (t: IncomingTransaction) => [t.date, t.amount, t.description].join("|");
```

Since currency isn't part of the key, two transactions that differ only by currency (e.g. the same date/amount/description, one EUR and one USD) hash to the same key and the second one is dropped as a duplicate before it ever reaches the exporter. This went unnoticed until currency was added to transactions in 3.2.0. The fix should include `currency` in the dedupe key.
